correctness.rationale: For fixed h>0,k1,k2,F real, the potential quartic has depressed shift s=-k2/(3h). With A=[4(E-K0)/h]^(1/4), centered u=(x-s)/A, the energy polynomial is 1-u^4-epsilon u^2-eta u with epsilon=O(A^-2), eta=O(A^-3). Its two simple moving turning roots factor with a positive quadratic. Substitution u=m+d sin(theta) turns physical-time Abel integrals into analytic bounded parameter integrals. Symmetry at eta=0 gives J_u=0 and analytic odd response O(eta), so mean x=s+O(A^-2). Period T=2sqrt2 a_h I E^-1/4[1+O(E^-1/2)]. The signed original-x residence threshold u=-s/A yields leading coefficient s/(A I), with O(A^-3) remainder. Therefore the limits E^(1/4)T and E^(1/4) signed fraction determine a_h then h=4/a_h^4 and k2=-3hs. A common regular theta-coupling bounds W1 distance from the quartic-oscillator occupation density by O(A^-2)=O(E^-1/2). Independent check: Independently integrated the original physical-time quartic turning-point quadratures for (k1,k2,h,F)=(1,2,3,0.7) and energies 100,10000,1000000. Obtained E^1/4 T≈3.98451965 at E=10^6 versus predicted 3.9846658 and scaled signed imbalance≈-0.15774534 versus -0.15773954. Independently checked depressed-quartic algebra and limiting density normalization. Numerical quadrature is corroboration, not infinite-E proof.
residual_risks: Conservative undamped and unforced-in-time scalar quartic at fixed h>0 and E→∞; k1 and load F cannot be recovered from these two leading limits.
